newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Atlas Copco bids for Prime Service. [CORRECTED 14:35 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Atlas Copco bids for Prime Service. [CORRECTED 14:35 GMT]

text.p: Swedish industrial engineer Atlas Copco said on Monday it was bidding seven billion crowns, or $900 million, for U.S. machinery leasing group Prime Service Inc.
Atlas Copco said in a statement that its bid of $32 a share had been approved by Prime Service's board.

Following an agreement between the two companies, Atlas Copco said it would start a cash tender offer on June 9 for all of Prime Service's 28 million or so shares which would run for 20 business days. The transaction was expected to close in the third quarter of 1997.
"The board of directors of both Prime Service and Atlas Copco have approved the transaction," the statement said.
The acquisition is subject to anti-trust approvals and other customary conditions.
Atlas Copco's chief executive Giulio Mazzalupi said the acquisition increased the group's opportunity to develop its business in the U.S. and enhance growth potential.
"Atlas Copco will also achieve a leading position in service of construction and industrial equipment in the U.S.," Mazzalupi said.

Atlas Copco said the acquisition would positively affect cash flow per share from the first full operational year although earnings per share would decrease during the first two years by a maximum of five percent.
The acquisition would be financed through a mixture of cash, commercial paper and banklines.
Prime Service was acquired in December 1994 by Investcorp, certain international investors and Prime Service management.
The company completed an initial public offering in October 1996.

"Investcorp and the other international investors, who currently own about 74 percent of the outstanding shares of Prime Service, have agreed to tender all of their shares as part of the Atlas Copco acquisition," the statement said.
A bid of $32 a share represents a 28 percent premium over current share price of Prime on June 6.

Prime Service is the second largest equipment rental company in the U.S., currently operating 122 rental equipment locations in 14 states and rents over 100 different types of equipment. It has about 2,000 staff.
Total revenue in 1996 was about $330 million with an operating profit of $66 million (corrects from $73 million).
After 45 minutes of trading at 0845 GMT, Atlas Copco shares were two crowns higher at 211.5 while the Stockholm general index was 0.85 percent higher.
